issues: The label “Mormon” does not match the established character label “Mormon (young)” for this account; the text identifies him as Mormon, so the intended identity is clear.

“Ammaron came to Mormon when Mormon was about ten years old” compresses the source’s approximate timing: Ammaron came about the time he hid up the records, while Mormon was about ten. The scene should preserve that this timing is approximate.

The summary’s “take the plates of Nephi” and “engrave what he has observed” are future instructions, not actions in the scene; the notes and prohibitions correctly flag this distinction. Keep the scene to the conversation.
The dialogue excerpts are verbatim and contiguous; narration is empty. The preceding scene’s record-making is not improperly merged into this conversation.
The character label “Mormon (young)” conveys an age the scene does not specify; verse 1:5 gives descent and parentage but no age.

The scene compresses events: Mormon’s arrival at Zarahemla at age eleven (verse 6) and the land’s described condition (verse 7) are reported consecutively, not necessarily simultaneous. Depict them as separate or use a non-specific representation.
The character label “Mormon’s father” is supported by the verse, but is not the established label “Mormon (young)” or a named character.

The scene title says war “begins near Zarahemla,” while the source says the war began among them at the borders of Zarahemla by Sidon; the framing should not imply a battle action or a more specific site.

The summary combines gathering and multiple battles within the same year; they are reported in sequence and should not be compressed into one moment. Specific battle action is permitted only as a conservative depiction of the reported battles; avoid adding weapons or other unspecified details.
The summary says the Lamanites “withdraw their design,” but the verse does not explain the design; avoid implying a particular plan or negotiation.
The narration excerpt “knew of the goodness of Jesus.” is not a contiguous exact excerpt: the verse reads “tasted and knew of the goodness of Jesus.” Use a verbatim excerpt.

The summary states that Mormon remained among the people and that the land was cursed, events the verse reports in sequence; do not present them as a single simultaneous scene or depict the curse visibly.

The scene combines the robbers’ infestation, inhabitants hiding treasure, and the treasure’s slipperiness, which the verse relates in sequence; avoid implying all occur simultaneously or inventing a specific robbery.
The summary says the events “fulfill” the words of Abinadi and Samuel; this is supported by the verse, but they are cited in narration and should not be shown as present.
